questions.enonce_markdown:
What is:

(i) Digestion,

(ii) Absorption,

(iii) Assimilation? *(4, 2, 3 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Digestion** is the **breakdown of large, insoluble food molecules into small, soluble molecules** that can be absorbed, by mechanical action (chewing) and by **enzymes** (chemical digestion).

(ii) **Absorption** is the **passage of digested food (soluble) molecules from the alimentary canal into the blood or lymph**, mainly through the villi of the ileum.

(iii) **Assimilation** is the **use of the absorbed food by the body cells** to build new protoplasm and tissues, for growth and repair, or to release energy.

questions.enonce_markdown: Describe the digestion of protein in mammals. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Proteins are digested by **protease enzymes** into **amino acids**, in three regions of the alimentary canal:

1. **Stomach**: the walls secrete **gastric juice** containing **hydrochloric acid** and the enzyme **pepsin**. The acid gives the acid medium (about pH 2) required by pepsin and kills bacteria. **Pepsin** breaks the proteins down into **peptides (polypeptides)**. (Rennin, in young mammals, clots the milk protein.)
2. **Duodenum**: **bile** from the liver neutralizes the acid and makes the medium alkaline. The **pancreatic juice** contains the enzyme **trypsin**, which continues to break down proteins and polypeptides into **smaller peptides**.
3. **Ileum**: the **intestinal juice** contains **peptidases (erepsin)**, which break the peptides into **amino acids**.

**Summary:** protein $\xrightarrow{\text{pepsin (stomach), trypsin (duodenum)}}$ peptides $\xrightarrow{\text{erepsin (ileum)}}$ amino acids. The amino acids are then absorbed into the blood.

questions.enonce_markdown: How is the ileum adapted to its absorptive functions? *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The ileum is adapted for absorption because:

1. It is **very long** (about 6 m in man), which gives a **large surface area** and enough time for absorption.
2. Its inner wall is **folded and covered with numerous finger-like villi**, which greatly increase the surface area; the epithelium cells also have **microvilli**.
3. The wall of each villus is **very thin (one cell thick)**, so that digested food diffuses quickly across it.
4. Each villus has a **dense network of blood capillaries**, which carry away glucose, amino acids, vitamins and mineral salts and **maintain a steep concentration gradient**.
5. Each villus has a **lacteal (lymph vessel)**, which absorbs fatty acids and glycerol.
6. The **muscles of the wall** contract (**peristalsis**) to mix the food with the juices and bring it into contact with the villi; the wall is kept **moist**.
